summary: All acceptance criteria met and re-verified: 8 nlp_rules tests + 7 live multi-item tests + 48-test backend suite pass, frontend build/lint clean, 6-language UI with full key parity, auth/CORS/admin-key untouched, whisper import stays lazy.

findings.detail: An additive, nullable `submission_id` column plus an idempotent SQLite migration were added to the complaints table. This is the designed mechanism for the one-row-per-item multi-item persistence described in context.json key_patterns (MultiComplaintResponse{submission_id,...}), and it alters no existing column or auth, so it does not fail any acceptance criterion. Noted only because the brief said 'no DB schema change' — informational, no action required. If a strict no-column-additions reading is intended by the task owner, this would need revisiting, but the task's own architecture requires submission_id and the migration is safe/idempotent.
